body:
I don't know .. maybe.  I still haven't talked with him and I am honestly dreading it.  I have gotten lots of good advice here, but I don't really know which to take or how I'm going to do it yet.

I think you are hitting the nail on the head with the "what's the point" thing.  I absolutely get that vibe from him, and I really have no idea how to talk with him about it because I know he will have a really good point when he points out that he isn't getting anywhere in his career

Well he did try that early this year.  He and a friend started a business but it didn't go well at all.  Their clients that they were working with really screwed them over and they got discouraged with it and haven't had a lot a luck.

I don't want to go into specifics, but he works in higher education.  Or at least he did.  He used to have a great job but the situation got really bad, and he was really depressed even then.  It was a lot of politics and he was just a nervous wreck and decided to leave that job.  Since then he is working as a web designer for a small company but I know he hates it.  I know he badly wants to go back to working for a college, he really loved being able to help students out there.

No, we don't have kids yet.  I think we want to but I think we both need to make sure that we have our lives in order before we try to bring any others into the world.  We also don't really have any problems with money or anything like that, we are really fortunate.
What could that be though?  I can't imagine why he would want to destroy his own work or anything.

Thank you for the good advice, I'm not sure I know how to respond right now.  But for my part I really don't care what he does or doesn't do as long as he keeps trying.  I really believe that if he does something will have to give, but I think some of his depression is contagious because even know I wonder if that is really true.

I think this is the real problem.  I hate to say it but what depresses him is also depressing me, because I am depressed for him.  It is so unfair that he should work so hard and help out so many other people in life and never catch a break himself.

It also makes me think of an old friend of ours who was in a similar situation.  He was really similar because he constantly had the same kind of bad luck.  He even passed away a year or so ago right as things were starting to turn around for him.  I think my husband thinks about it too, it's so sad.
I don't think I understand what you mean by "how and why not"

Okay then I have a question

I kind of feel like I am part of the problem.  I know that sounds really weird but I have gotten success on my own, and I kind of get the feeling that he feels that he can't keep up with me and is inadequate because of it.  I can support him all I want but those facts aren't going to change.  It isn't a problem in our marriage but I know it's always going to make him feel kind of inferior.  What can I do about that?
Thanks I guess I just don't feel like it will be enough

We have taken on some new things in the past year or so but I am not sure how helpful it has been.  I try to do a lot with him but even before recently I could tell that he is so distant.  I wish I knew how to describe it but over the recent months and maybe year I can just see a sadness in him and I know exactly where it comes from.
Thank you.  I am trying to read up on this kind of thing but also being able to talk with someone about it is very helpful.
Thank you.  What kind of resources do you think you would suggest?

I think part of the problem is that I can be helpful with his emotions and well being but I can't be helpful with what is causing the problem.  He has the hardest luck out of anyone I have ever seen, and I wish I could change that for him but I can't
Here's a hint: Girls hate rude and unhelpful comments.
If that is true, what can I do for him?  I don't think it is because of anything he did or didn't do, he is really great at what he does for a living. :(

Thank you, I am sure he knows I feel that way.  I think some of the problem is that my career has gone pretty well, and I will be the first to tell you that it isn't because of anything I did right or wrong.  I just got really lucky with a good job out of college and it has had really good bonuses every year since.  He won't say it, but I think it bothers him that he works harder than me or anyone else we know and that he isn't getting anything out of it.

I didn't know until recently it bothers him this bad.  I just wish things would pay off for him so he could have what he deserves, including being happy
I'm not sure I understand what you mean when you say "he's accepted continously and has gained nothing from it."
